## Scope and exact theorem

Subproblem C66-GEO-Z only: construct and identify the evaluation-failure locus Z in the balanced tetragonal Casnati–Ekedahl geometry of packet C66-001-v3. The campaign exact target W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q)≅W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21) being ⊕Q(8) is not claimed here. No dependency artifacts are supplied (TASK.json: blocked_dependencies=[], dependency_artifacts={}), so nothing is imported from later DAG nodes C66-GEO-H0, C66-GEO-COMP, or Tate/counterexample nodes.

Blocked routes vcd-only-vanishing, undecorated-cgp-top-weight-graph-complex, point-count-without-degree-parity-separation, and forgetful-map-renaming-local-system-unknown are not used. Working-context candidates are treated as unproved and are not cited as evidence.

## Source-backed inputs

1. Packet CE convention and balanced splitting (C66-001-v3 canonical geometric bottleneck): F=O_{P^1}(4)⊕O_{P^1}(5); W_5:=(O_{P(E^∨)}(2)⊗γ^*O_{P^1}(-5))|_C is the f_2=5 summand of (O(2)⊗γ^*F^∨)|_C, not the O_{P^1}(5) summand of F; six-point failure condition stated as O_C(Γ)≅W_5⊗ω_C^{-1}; ordered distinct reduced divisors modeled as a finite étale S_6-cover of the reduced-support open (explicitly not closed).

2. SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 (packet primary locator): for W_f=(O_{P(E^∨)}(2)⊗γ^*O(-f))|_C one has deg(W_f|_C)=4g+12−4f, the obstruction splits as H^0(ω_C⊗W^∨(Γ))=⊕_i H^0(ω_C⊗W_{f_i}^∨(Γ)), and deg(ω_C⊗W_f^∨(Γ))=4f+n−2g−14.

3. FND-0001 (mechanically_verified): for d=3g−3+n, W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{g,n})≅W_{2d−16}H^{2d−16}(M_{g,n})(d). Used only as ambient dictionary; not needed for the geometric identification of Z.

4. FND-0005 (corroborated for (6,6)): proposed evaluation-failure locus nonempty by the indicated Riemann–Roch computation, subject to the independent confirmation recorded in (E) below.

## Proved steps

### Step 1: Degree arithmetic for g=6

Substitute g=6 into SRC-0004: deg(W_5)=4·6+12−4·5=16 and deg(W_4)=4·6+12−4·4=20. With deg(ω_C)=2g−2=10 one obtains deg(L)=deg(W_5⊗ω_C^{-1})=16−10=6.

For n=6 and an effective degree-six divisor Γ, SRC-0004 gives

deg(ω_C⊗W_5^∨(Γ))=4·5+6−2·6−14=0,

deg(ω_C⊗W_4^∨(Γ))=4·4+6−2·6−14=−4.

### Step 2: Vanishing of the f=4 obstruction (claim A)

On a smooth projective connected curve, a line bundle of negative degree has H^0=0. Hence H^0(C,ω_C⊗W_4^∨(Γ))=0 for every effective degree-six Γ on every smooth geometric fibre. The CE obstruction therefore reduces entirely to the f=5 summand.

### Step 3: f=5 obstruction criterion (claim B)

The line bundle ω_C⊗W_5^∨(Γ) has degree zero. On a smooth projective connected curve, a degree-zero line bundle has a nonzero global section if and only if it is isomorphic to O_C. Equivalently,

H^0(C,ω_C⊗W_5^∨(Γ))≠0  ⇔  ω_C⊗W_5^∨(Γ)≅O_C  ⇔  O_C(Γ)≅W_5⊗ω_C^{-1}=L.

This is exactly the packet six-point failure condition, derived from the f_2=5 summand of SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 including the sign in γ^*O(−5).

### Step 4: Set-theoretic identification Z^{geo}=I^{geo} (claim C)

By Steps 2–3 and the splitting of the CE obstruction in SRC-0004,

H^0(C,ω_C⊗W^∨(Γ))≠0  ⇔  H^0(C,ω_C⊗W_5^∨(Γ))≠0  ⇔  O_C(Γ)≅L.

Therefore the geometric evaluation-failure locus Z^{geo} coincides set-theoretically with the Abel–Jacobi incidence locus I^{geo} of geometric points of Conf_6 (or of the relative effective-divisor space) satisfying O_C(Γ)≅L. This is the identification required by C66-GEO-Z at the geometric-point level.

### Step 5: Reduced-support open and finite étale S_6-cover (claim D)

In the relative effective-divisor space of degree six over B^{bal}, the condition that the support be six distinct reduced points is the complement of the relative discriminant (non-reduced or coincident support). That complement is open; it is not closed. Over that open, the map from the stack of six ordered pairwise-distinct sections to the unordered reduced divisor is a principal S_6-bundle (finite étale S_6-torsor): the S_6-action freely permutes ordered distinct labels. Consequently the ordered reduced failure locus is the preimage of the reduced-support open of the residual incidence for L, matching the packet model. (On coarse moduli spaces with residual automorphisms the freeness may fail; the torsor statement is on the stack of pairwise-distinct sections, as required by the packet bottleneck.)

### Step 6: Fibrewise nonemptiness of |L| (claim E)

Riemann–Roch on a smooth genus-6 fibre: χ(L)=deg(L)−g+1=6−6+1=1, so h^0(L)=1+h^1(L)≥1. Thus |L| is nonempty on every smooth geometric fibre, and the unordered residual incidence is fibrewise nonempty. This independently confirms the nonemptiness content of FND-0005 at the level of residual linear systems. Nonemptiness of the reduced-support open on every fibre is not claimed: when h^0(L) jumps or all residual divisors are non-reduced, reduced ordered points may fail on special fibres; denseness of reduced support on free-pencil fibres is deferred to C66-GEO-H0 / C66-GEO-COMP.

## Explicitly not proved (gaps)

G1. Scheme-theoretic equality of the determinantal/Fitting CE rank-drop scheme with the Abel–Jacobi incidence scheme (nilpotents, multiplicities, obstruction complexes). Geometric-point agreement yields only reduced-support coincidence.

G2. Identification W_5≅ω_C^{⊗2}(−D) via relative duality O_{P(E^∨)}(1)|_C≅ω_C⊗γ^*O(2) (residual form Γ∈|ω_C(−D)|, D+Γ canonical). Useful for interpretation but not required for the obstruction identification of Z^{geo}.

G3. h^0(L)-stratification of the relative linear system; components, dimensions, stabilizers, unbalanced CE splittings, hyperelliptic/trigonal special loci; maps to tetragonal moduli (C66-GEO-H0, C66-GEO-COMP).

G4. Any Tate-type, Gysin, or survival statement for W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) or for codimension-13 contributions supported on a closed stratified Z (C66-TATE-*, C66-CEX-*).

G5. Constancy of relative dimension 2 (P^2-bundle) over all of balanced tetragonal moduli: h^0(ω_C(−D))=3 requires h^0(O_C(D))=2 and fails where the pencil jumps.

## Computational hypotheses

None. No experiment is used; finite experiments cannot close a proof.

## Downstream handoff

The geometric object for later nodes is: residual incidence for L=W_5⊗ω_C^{-1} over balanced tetragonal CE data, with ordered reduced model a finite étale S_6-cover of an open (not closed) reduced-support locus, and with CE failure controlled solely by the f=5 summand.

parsed_artifact.theorem_statement: Let g=6 and let B^{bal} be any base carrying a smooth family of genus-6 curves with a balanced tetragonal Casnati–Ekedahl structure (relations bundle F≅O_{P^1}(4)⊕O_{P^1}(5)), universal curve π:C→B^{bal}, and CE line bundles W_f:=(O_{P(E^∨)}(2)⊗γ^*O_{P^1}(-f))|_C for f∈{4,5} (packet convention: W_5 is the f_2=5 summand of (O(2)⊗γ^*F^∨)|_C, not the O_{P^1}(5) summand of F). Write L:=W_5⊗ω_{C/B}^{-1}. Let Conf_6(C/B^{bal}) be the relative stack of six ordered pairwise-distinct sections, with associated relative divisor Γ, and let Z^{geo}⊂Conf_6 be the geometric evaluation-failure locus consisting of geometric points at which the CE obstruction space H^0(C,ω_C⊗W^∨(Γ)) is nonzero. Then: (A) for every geometric fibre and every effective degree-six divisor Γ one has deg(ω_C⊗W_4^∨(Γ))=−4, hence H^0(C,ω_C⊗W_4^∨(Γ))=0; (B) for every such Γ one has deg(ω_C⊗W_5^∨(Γ))=0, and H^0(C,ω_C⊗W_5^∨(Γ))≠0 if and only if O_C(Γ)≅L; (C) consequently Z^{geo} coincides set-theoretically with the Abel–Jacobi incidence locus I^{geo} of geometric points satisfying O_C(Γ)≅L; (D) the locus of reduced-support degree-six effective divisors in the relative effective-divisor space is open (not closed), and the forgetful map from Conf_6 to that reduced-support open is a finite étale S_6-torsor on the stack of pairwise-distinct sections, so the ordered reduced failure locus is the preimage of the reduced-support open of the residual incidence for L; (E) on every smooth geometric fibre, χ(L)=1, hence h^0(L)≥1, so the residual linear system |L| is nonempty and the unordered residual incidence is fibrewise nonempty. This identifies the geometric evaluation-failure locus for the balanced tetragonal CE geometry of packet C66-001-v3; it does not assert scheme-theoretic equality of Fitting/determinantal ideals with the Abel–Jacobi ideal, does not stratify by h^0(L), and does not claim Tate type of any contribution to W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q).
